item.title: Is Hezbollah Still a Threat?
item.description: Any U.S. successes against Iran can also help undermine Hezbollah. CSIS's Daniel Byman addresses key questions about Hezbollah's influence in Foreign Affairs.

item.description: Iran possesses the largest and most diverse missile arsenal in the Middle East. The CSIS Missile Defense Project unpacks Iran's current missile activity and capabilities.

item.title: Macron’s Île-Longue Speech: Updating France’s Nuclear Doctrine for a New Era
item.description: President Macron’s updated doctrine marks a watershed for European defense, with an increased French nuclear arsenal and a “forward deterrence” strategy that integrates regional conventional capabilities. It aims to provide the operational means for strategic autonomy.

item.title: How Will Cyber Warfare Shape the U.S.-Israel Conflict with Iran?
item.description: The U.S.-Israeli strikes on Iran were accompanied by cyber operations targeting Iranian apps, news sites, and government services. Iran will retaliate, and cyberspace is likely where that response will unfold.

item.title: Why Decapitation Will Not Solve the United States’ Iran Problem
item.description: Killing Iran's top leaders may feel like a decisive blow, but history shows that decapitation rarely produces the political outcomes the United States hopes for, and often exacerbates instability.

item.title: U.S.-India Insight: Indian States China + 1 Strategy: Aim Lower to go Bigger
item.description: State governments have critical roles to play in helping India build a better business environment. In 2025, most state policies focus on specific sectors like electronics or data centers.
